Practice 1 Main · count

How many structural isomers (alcohols and ethers) has C₄H₁₀O?

Show answer
  1. Degrees of unsaturation of C4H10O = 0.
  2. Listing the skeletons systematically and placing the group on every non-equivalent position gives the isomers drawn below.
  3. Answer: 7.
1. 3° alcohol 2. 1° alcohol 3. 2° alcohol 4. 1° alcohol 5. ether
6. ether 7. ether

Practice 24 Main · E/Z

Assign E or Z to the alkene shown: C₂ carries CH₂OH and H; C₃ carries C(CH₃)₃ and OH; CH₂OH and C(CH₃)₃ are on the same side.

Show answer
  1. At C-2: CH₂OH > H (CIP). At C-3: OH > C(CH₃)₃.
  2. The higher-priority groups CH₂OH and OH lie on the opposite side of the double bond.
  3. E.
  4. Note: CH₂OH and C(CH₃)₃ are cis/trans-related in the opposite sense to the E/Z label; "cis/trans" (same group on the same side) and E/Z do not always agree.

  2. The higher-priority groups CH₂Br and CH₂Br lie on the opposite side of the double bond.
  3. E.
  4. Note: CONH₂ and CH₂Br are cis/trans-related in the opposite sense to the E/Z label; "cis/trans" (same group on the same side) and E/Z do not always agree.

Practice 46 Main · geometrical

How many geometrical isomers are possible for CH₃–(CH=CH)1–CH₃ with n = 1 double bonds?

Show answer
  1. Each C=C can be E or Z (end groups differ on each carbon), so n = 1 stereogenic double bonds.
  2. Symmetrical chain: (2n + 2⌈n/2⌉)/2 = (2 + 2)/2 = 2.
  3. Answer: 2 (confirmed by enumerating the structure).

Practice 55 Main · ring

How many stereoisomers does 1,2-dimethylcyclopentane have, and how many of them are optically active?

Show answer
  1. The ring has two stereogenic ring carbons carrying CH₃ and H. cis and trans isomers are possible.
  2. Mirror-plane test: cis is achiral (meso); trans is a pair of enantiomers.
  3. 3 stereoisomers, of which 2 are optically active (one enantiomeric pair).

Practice 60 Main · tautomerism

Can acetone show keto–enol tautomerism?

Practice 169 Main · counting

How many stereoisomers (total) does 2,3,4-trichloropentane have? How many of them are optically active?

Show answer
  1. Stereogenic units found: 3 stereocentre(s).
  2. The naive count 23 = 8 is reduced by symmetry/ring constraints (meso or identical forms) to 4.
  3. Enumerating and removing duplicates/identical forms: 4 stereoisomers in all: 2 chiral (1 enantiomeric pair) and 2 achiral (meso/cis-trans type).
  4. Optically active: 2.

] A solution of 1.5 g of an optically active compound in 25 mL of solvent, examined in a 10 cm polarimeter tube, rotates the plane of polarised light by +1.65°. Calculate the specific rotation.

Show answer

  2. [α] = α/(l c) = +1.65/(1 × 0.06) = +27.5° (deg dm-1 g-1 mL).

Practice 227 Main · Baeyer strain

Calculate the Baeyer angle strain (deviation per bond) for planar cyclopropane (tetrahedral angle 109°28′).

Show answer
  1. Planar internal angle = 180(n − 2)/n = 60°.
  2. d = ½(109°28′ − 60°) = 24.73° = +24°44′.
  3. Positive deviation: bonds must be compressed (angle strain).

Show answer

  3. Positive deviation: bonds must be compressed (angle strain).

Practice 230 Main · Baeyer strain

Calculate the Baeyer angle strain (deviation per bond) for planar cyclohexane (tetrahedral angle 109°28′).

Show answer
  1. Planar internal angle = 180(n − 2)/n = 120°.
  2. d = ½(109°28′ − 120°) = -5.27° = −5°16′.
  3. Negative deviation: a planar ring would need angles larger than tetrahedral; real cyclohexane puckers into the strain-free chair, so Baeyer's planar assumption fails.

Show answer
  1. Planar internal angle = 180(n − 2)/n = 128.57°.
  2. d = ½(109°28′ − 128.57°) = -9.55° = −9°33′.
  3. Negative deviation: a planar ring would need angles larger than tetrahedral; real cyclohexane puckers into the strain-free chair, so Baeyer's planar assumption fails.

Practice 252 Main · S_{N}2

2-bromobutane (SN2) is treated with OH⁻. Draw the product and give its CIP configuration.

(R)
Show answer
  1. Substrate priorities: Br > C₂H₅ > CH₃ > H; configuration R.
  2. SN2 = backside attack: the arrangement of the other three groups is inverted.
  3. In the product the priorities are OH > C₂H₅ > CH₃ > H.
  4. Product configuration: S.
  5. The letter changes (R → S).
(S)

Practice 266 Main · allene

Is the allene C₂H₅(CH₃)C=C=C(Br)C₂H₅ optically active (chiral)?

Show answer
  1. An allene X(a)(b)C=C=C(c)(d) is chiral only if a ≠ b and c ≠ d.
  2. Here the end groups are (C₂H₅, CH₃) and (Br, C₂H₅): both ends have two different groups.
  3. Yes, it is axially chiral (optically active, resolvable).

Practice 278 Main · biaryl

A biphenyl carries ortho substituents H, H on one ring (positions 2 and 6) and COOH, F on the other (2′ and 6′); all other ring positions carry H. Can it be resolved into stable enantiomers at room temperature? (Assume that F, H, OH, OCH₃ are too small to block rotation, and that three or more bulky ortho groups are needed.)

Show answer
  1. Axis test: ring 1 has (H, H) (identical); ring 2 has (COOH, F) (different).
  2. Bulky ortho groups (CH₃, NO₂, COOH, Br): 1.
  3. No: ring symmetry (a = b or c = d) makes the molecule achiral.

Show answer
  1. Axis test: ring 1 has (CH₃, F) (different); ring 2 has (Br, CH₃) (different).
  2. Bulky ortho groups (CH₃, NO₂, COOH, Br): 3.
  3. Yes: chiral axis and hindered rotation (≥ 3 bulky ortho groups).

Practice 286 Main · chair

In the chair drawn, ring carbons are numbered 1 to 6 starting at the right-hand tip and going to the back. The substituent on C-1 is CH₃ (equatorial) and that on C-2 is OH (equatorial). Are they cis or trans?

Show answer
  1. Work out which face each substituent is on: an axial group is on the face its axial bond points to; an equatorial group is on the face opposite to the axial bond of the same carbon (axial bonds alternate up, down, up... around the ring).
  2. C-1: equatorial → down face; C-2: equatorial → up face.
  3. Same face = cis, opposite faces = trans: trans.
  4. After a ring flip the groups become axial and axial, but the cis/trans relationship does not change.
